A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEAR study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector evaluations in Tables 1–2, robustness and diagnostic experiments in Tables 4–8, and ablations in Figures 8–9.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the benchmark comparisons and appendix robustness analyses and ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use inpainting-based RAD scoring, bilateral channel pruning and linear-classifier refinement with a frozen backbone. V1 already specifies refinement using both original and inpainted data. V2 reconciles Algorithm 1 with that description and supplies implementation details, without establishing a new method component.

E1.justification: Training sources, the nine-generator evaluation, three in-the-wild benchmarks and appendix test groups are retained. Table 6's 'GAN avg (6 models)' becomes 'Non-diffusion avg (6 models)'; v2 identifies the existing constituents, including SAN and SITD, rather than adding new coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables and appendix experiments, including Corvi/Rajan, their Stay-Positive variants and the inpaint-trained ablation variants. Reclassifying DRCT as CNN-based corrects its description without changing the evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The retained experiments keep the same data counts, metrics, backbones and pruning search range. V2 newly documents augmentation order, selected pruning ratios and DEAR-r's effective batch of 128 after pairing; Table 9 retains the nominal 64/64 batch specification. These clarify existing settings without establishing a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The WEBP analysis, unseen-generator study, alternative-inpainter comparison, channel-ranking consistency analysis and inpaint-training/pruning-ratio ablations already appear in v1. V2 clarifies their descriptions but adds no distinct analysis or ablation; the Table 6 numerical correction is assessed under E6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Table 8 retains the same Spearman correlation and Jaccard similarity reporting.

E6.justification: Table 6 corrects DEAR-r's FLUX F.Acc from 100.00% to 96.60% and its improvement from +88.00 to +84.60 points, matching Table 1. Table 1 changes ClipDet original R.Acc from 85.4 to 85.3, post-processed C2P-CLIP from 96.5 to 96.6 and post-processed DEAR-c from 76.5 to 76.4. Table 2 changes Corvi+ original LOKI R.Acc from 99.2 to 99.1. Overall findings remain stable.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds an explicit soft-occupancy definition of RAD's regional means in Equation 9, accommodating fractional boundary contributions beyond Equation 4's binary-region formulation. Algorithm 1 also corrects score normalization and fractional-percentile conversion. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about prediction asymmetry, bilateral pruning and robustness to unseen generators and post-processing. The conclusion's more explicit description of inpaint-augmented classifier refinement restates an existing component.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly explains how empty prompts avoid prompt-specific semantic shortcuts and how crop-dependent labels provide localized supervision. Appendix C.2 qualifies the previously described GAN family as a mixed non-diffusion group. The central spurious-feature interpretation and Appendix B limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands reproducibility information: empty prompts, soft versus hard masks, bilinear mask downsampling, crop handling, selected pruning ratios, BatchNorm behavior, initialization, paired batches, crop labels, loss combination and ordered augmentation parameters. Algorithm 1 and Table 9 are correspondingly clarified. Appendices C and F also identify test-set provenance and real-image splits, including RedCaps pairing for LOKI.

R1.justification: Section 5 revises historical attribution, distinguishing early CNN detection work by Wang et al. from later upsampling analysis by Tan et al. Section 4.1 explicitly attributes the adopted test set to Rajan et al. The cited-work inventory and DEAR's positioning relative to Stay-Positive remain essentially unchanged; publication-metadata updates do not add new works.

P1.justification: V2 expands explanatory prose mainly in Appendix E and the appendix dataset descriptions, shortens Section 4.3 and corrects terminology, cross-references and bibliographic details. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves to the following page, Figure 4's caption corrects the swapped axis descriptions, and Figure 8's caption clarifies the plotted pruning values. Table 6 is relabeled, Table 9 gains implementation rows, and table highlighting and placement change. The figures retain their plotted evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through the expanded Appendix E and more consistent Algorithm 1. Correcting Table 6 to match Table 1, fixing Figure 4's axis description and clarifying dataset composition also improve internal consistency. These are useful refinements to an otherwise substantially unchanged study, with the central empirical evidence and conclusions retained.
